guide.title: Lighting
guide.caption: White light and saved scenes
guide.text:
Use Lights on and Lights off on Home for everyday lighting.

Room tools → Lighting brings White light, Scenes, Programmes and Channels together. Opening a tab does not change the lights.

Last confirmed shows the most recent controller readback and its age. If a result is unconfirmed, do not repeat it. Check connection reads current lighting without changing it; ask the room host if controls stay unavailable.

guide.title: Room controls
guide.caption: Lighting, blinds and preferences
guide.text:
Home opens the everyday room page. Opening a page does not change the lights.

Lift blinds, Open slats and Close & lower are on Home. Movement is locked by default and requires a connected controller. Screen & controls explains availability and saves whether the controls are shown.

Room tools also holds appearance, screen and weather preferences. If equipment controls stay unavailable, ask the room host.

guide.title: Experiment instructions
guide.caption: Instructions, markers and recording
guide.text:
Experiment mode guides a repeatable sequence of instructions and saves panel annotations.

It does not start a recorder. Arrange recording separately. An experiment must reserve lighting before it starts, then close its workers and return verified everyday control when finished.

Room tools → System & help shows room service availability. Availability alone does not prove usable sensor data.

guide.title: Connection & help
guide.caption: Panel, services and weather
guide.text:
Beta and the room-network website share one controller. Join the room Wi-Fi before opening the website; the guide shows the connection details.

The lighting status explains when controls are ready, reserved for an experiment, checking or unconfirmed. Website offline means the page cannot reach the panel. Open System & help for guidance.

Weather is an outdoor model estimate, separate from indoor measurements. Source details are under Room tools → Date & weather.

guide.title: A room for research
guide.caption: Lighting, sensing and shared space
guide.text:
The Smart Conference Room brings lighting and several kinds of sensors into one shared space. Researchers compare their different views to study presence, movement and the room environment.

Ceiling sensors measure distance or light colour. Four Azure Kinect cameras provide colour, depth and infrared reference views for comparing sensors.

This tour starts no equipment or recording. A sensor appearing on the map does not mean it is currently connected or recording.

guide.title: Lighting & colour
guide.caption: Ten lights, eight channels
guide.text: Ten lights mix eight channels into white light and colour scenes. Gradient spreads colour across the room. Values are drive settings, not measured brightness.

guide.title: Distance & colour sensors
guide.caption: COMBO, IRMA and Color
guide.text:
COMBO combines a coarse 8 × 8 distance grid with light-colour sensing. It times reflected light to estimate distance.

IRMA Matrix gives a denser 25 × 20 distance view and reflected-signal strength. It measures distance, not body heat.

Color sensors track light-colour changes without taking a photograph. Raw values need calibration for absolute measurements.

guide.title: Ceiling map
guide.caption: Explore the sensor families
guide.text: Select a sensor family to see its registered ceiling positions.

ceiling_map.title: Ceiling sensor map
ceiling_map.caption: Choose a family, then tap a marker for its name, reference ID and sensor details.
ceiling_map.orientation: Reference grid: R1–R14 along the long axis; C1–C5 across. The displayed origin is at the lower left.
ceiling_map.note: Faint squares: light troffers; slatted squares: HVAC vents; crosses: sprinklers. Approximate positions; symbols do not show size or live status. Four side-mounted Color sensors omitted.

families.label: Color
families.description: TCS34725 sensors measure red, green, blue and clear light channels. These ceiling sensors observe changes in room light; they do not form a camera image.

families.label: COMBO
families.description: STM32WB55 board with VL53L8CX 8 × 8 time-of-flight distances and TCS3430 XYZ/IR light-channel readings.

families.label: IRMA
families.description: IRMA MATRIX time-of-flight sensors return 25 × 20 distance samples. Their depth observations support room-surface and movement studies.

fixtures_source.note: Tile-level annotations; symbols do not represent measured footprints or live status.

help.title: Lighting
help.text: Check connection reads current settings without changing the lights. If a result is unconfirmed, do not repeat the command; ask the room host. Experiment controls return after cleanup.

help.title: Power
help.text:
Low supply voltage can slow the Pi and affect storage reliability. Check its supply, cable and connector; a separately powered LCD does not rule out a Pi power problem.

Open the reference to distinguish current warnings from earlier ones. Do not hide warnings or repeatedly power-cycle. Shut down normally before changing power.

steps.title: Check power warnings
steps.why: Read the Pi firmware flags when the panel is slow or reports a power warning.
steps.expect: 0x0 means no flags. Nonzero can include earlier warnings; it does not always mean a fault is active now.

help.title: Ubuntu checks
help.text:
Use a Terminal on the Ubuntu room computer. These commands inspect state; they do not start devices.

ROS owns room controls. Status owns the TV display and its clients. Session presence alone does not prove health.
help.commands:
hostname

uptime

free -m

df -h /

tmux list-sessions

source /opt/ros/indigo/setup.bash

source ~/catkin_ws/devel/setup.bash

timeout 10 rosservice list

steps.title: Confirm the computer
steps.why: Check which computer this Terminal is connected to.
steps.expect: A host name. Confirm it is the room computer before continuing.

steps.title: Check running time and load
steps.why: See time since boot and recent system load.
steps.expect: Uptime and load averages. Load is not a CPU percentage.

steps.title: Check memory
steps.why: Inspect memory in MiB when the room computer feels slow.
steps.expect: Memory totals and available/free space. Cached memory is not automatically a problem.

steps.title: Check storage
steps.why: Check space on the root filesystem before collecting more data.
steps.expect: Filesystem size, used space, available space and use percentage.

steps.title: Inspect existing sessions
steps.why: Look for existing sessions before considering a service start.
steps.expect: Session names, or no server. A session name alone does not prove the service is healthy.

steps.title: Load the ROS environment
steps.why: Make the installed ROS tools available in this Terminal. This does not start ROS.
steps.expect: Usually no output. If the file is missing, stop and check the installed setup with staff.

steps.title: Load the room workspace
steps.why: Add the installed room packages to this Terminal after loading ROS.
steps.expect: Usually no output. Keep using the same Terminal for the next check.

steps.title: List advertised services
steps.why: Ask the configured ROS master for service names, with a ten-second time limit.
steps.expect: Service names, an error or a timeout. Names show registration, not working sensors or devices.

help.title: Start services
help.text:
Room host only: stop experiments and check tmux sessions first. startROS.py replaces the ROS session; startStatus.py replaces Status. Do not use them as a quick connection fix.

Installed paths below are instructions only, not automatic recovery.
help.commands:
cd ~/catkin_ws/src/scr_control && python startROS.py

cd ~/scr.status_display && python startStatus.py

steps.title: Start the ROS session
steps.why: Only after studies are stopped, ownership is checked and the existing sessions are understood.
steps.expect: The launcher replaces the ROS session. Inspect its output and check services before using controls.

steps.title: Start the Status session
steps.why: Use only when the room host has decided the shared TV/Status session must be started.
steps.expect: The launcher replaces Status. Check the TV and required feeds; a session name is not a health check.

help.title: Restart computer
help.text:
Room host only: stop recordings and coordinate with other room users. Restarting interrupts shared controls and feeds.

Use the Ubuntu Restart action or its Terminal command below. After the desktop and network return, check ROS and Status; service autostart is not verified.

reference.effect: Room host only · interrupts shared work

steps.title: Restart the room computer
steps.why: Use after recordings have stopped and room users have coordinated the interruption.
steps.expect: The connection ends. Wait for the desktop/network, then check ROS and Status; autostart is not assured.
